comparator.sourceNotes: The current adopted TER (27 August 2026) controls the ordinary 180-EC pathway. First and second years each comprise eight compulsory 7.5-EC units. The third year is 15 EC university/approved personal minor + two faculty units at 7.5 each + one specialisation 7.5 + thesis seminar 7.5 + science communication 5 + thesis 10 = 60. The ordinary minor is offered by another faculty or faculties. The first two named faculty alternatives, Climate Change, End Times, Sustainability and Religion, Space and Place, are selected neutrally; the optional module is not added. Retain the previously selected Cultural and Political Impact of Religion specialisation under its broad academic-identity basis, independently of UCR fit; Origins of Religion is an unselected alternative. Quranic Arabic 1 plus an optional module is a mutually exclusive alternative to the ordinary 15-EC minor, not extra credit. Article 7.1 separately permits abroad, education and spiritual-care options of up to 30 EC and Board-approved course replacements; these conditioned alternatives do not turn the ordinary 15-EC faculty requirement into unrestricted minor space. Applicable degree total, approval and progress rules remain. English instruction remains supported. Current academic-year cover/interior and adopted date establish applicability despite a stale cover running line and concept metadata. The current formal choice clauses were freshly retrieved and visually inspected on 2026-10-08.

progressionAssessment.rationale: All 24 unique courses use an exact available cohort term and the only formal prerequisite, Law, Society & Justice for Comparative Constitutional Law, is completed three semesters earlier. PPD is in Year 1 and seven courses are level 300. Introductory philosophy, sociology, politics, archaeology and law precede the corresponding advanced interpretive, conflict, constitutional and heritage work where the timetable permits; the no-prerequisite civil-society course follows Introduction to Sociology.

alternativeSelection.assessment: One complete related-fields programme passes the evidence, coherence, course-contribution and schedule gates. The previous no-match incorrectly required a full religion-specific sequence before accepting any UCR response, even though the current contract permits an honest related-fields programme and the target explicitly combines religion with history, art history, politics, sociology, psychology and philosophy. A second environmental route would become a general sustainability curriculum because UCR lacks religion-and-climate or sacred-space content. Spiritual care/sexual health still lacks religious meaning frameworks and care practice, and education still lacks religion-teaching knowledge and didactics. No weaker second programme is added.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both study culturally active texts and their interpretation or transmission. UCR compares mythic literary traditions and text-image/oral movement; it does not provide the comparator's sustained religious-text theory or sacred-text scope.

African Art & Heritage directly studies visual forms carrying religious meaning. It supplies one regional heritage perspective rather than the comparator's broader iconographic study of sacred images.

Both develop philosophical analysis of belief, God, meaning and related questions. UCR's course is a general Western-philosophy introduction and does not reproduce the comparator's philosophy of religion and spirituality.
Both teach substantive ethical reasoning. UCR covers moral theories and applied ethics, but not the comparator's integrated religion, bioethics and care emphasis.
Both address political conflict and peacebuilding. UCR directly studies radicalisation, violence and reconciliation but is not a course in religion and politics.
UCR qualitative methodology is useful for community inquiry, but it is not a sufficiently direct counterpart to the comparator's religion-specific research-design course.
The comparator has a dedicated religion-specific thesis-design seminar; no scheduled UCR course reproduces that formation.
The comparator requires a credited 10-EC independent thesis in Religious Studies. UCR optional independent research is shown in parallel but remains outside the scheduled 180 EC.
The comparator's science communication is explicitly about communicating religion research; no scheduled UCR course is a sufficiently direct counterpart.
UCR contains religion-related cultural material but no sustained course in Christianity's history, sources and practice.
General humanities and social-science methods do not reproduce an introduction to the concepts and methods of Religious Studies.
The schedule has qualitative and social inquiry but no course in anthropology of religion.
World Myth & Literature and Philosophy of Mind include Indian or Buddhist material but do not provide a full course in South Asian religions.
No scheduled UCR course provides sustained study of Judaism's history, sources and practice.
General psychology and sociology courses support analysis of belief and identity but do not teach psychology and sociology of religion.
Mediterranean art history includes Islamic courts, but no scheduled UCR course provides sustained study of Islamic history, sources and practice.
No scheduled UCR course provides a sustained theory-and-practice study of religious ritual.
Media & Race supplies an identity-and-power lens, but it does not directly study religion, media and popular culture.
Sociology and social psychology address diversity and identity generally, but not new religious movements or lived religious diversity.
The comparator's genuine 15-EC university or approved personal minor remains visible without invented content.
General sustainability courses were not inserted merely to imitate a religion-and-climate option; the comparator's religious and spiritual framing remains unmatched.
UCR archaeology and environmental study do not reproduce the historical, sociological and spatial analysis of sacred space.
The complete UCR programme addresses selected cultural and political effects through related disciplines, but does not reproduce the comparator's religion-specific specialisation.

notes.text: Religious Studies at Groningen builds sustained knowledge of major traditions, lived religion, ritual, sacred texts and religion-specific methods. This UCR programme studies religion-related narratives and visual heritage and the cultural and political impact of belief through philosophy, law, sociology, psychology, politics, media and heritage. These are related perspectives rather than a substitute for the full Religious Studies sequence; Christianity, Judaism, Islam, South Asian traditions, ritual and religion-specific methods remain explicit gaps.
